title: Second Minimum Time to Reach Destination
summary: A city is modeled as a bi-directional graph with n vertices, each labeled from 1 to n.
statement: A city is modeled as a bi-directional graph with n vertices, each labeled from 1 to n. Edges are represented by a 2D array, where each entry indicates a bi-directional connection between two vertices. Each vertex has a traffic signal that alternates every change minutes. You can enter a vertex at any time but must leave only when the signal is green. The second minimum time to travel from vertex 1 to vertex n is sought, defined as the smallest value strictly greater than the minimum travel time. For example, the second minimum of [2, 3, 4] is 3, and for [2, 2, 4] it is 4. Given n, edges, time, and change, calculate the second minimum travel time. You can revisit any vertex multiple times, and the signals are green at the start of the journey.
constraints: The connected undirected graph has vertices 1 through n and equal edge traversal time.
All signals alternate green and red every change minutes in synchronization; departure is forbidden during red.
Return the smallest destination arrival time strictly greater than the minimum, allowing revisits.
hints: With equal edge times and synchronized signals, arrival time depends only on the number of traversed edges.
BFS while retaining the two distinct smallest step counts per vertex, then simulate signal waits for the destination’s second count.
Relax candidate steps into first or strictly-between second; for each edge wait to next green when current phase is red.
Two-distance BFS enumerates walk lengths in order; deterministic synchronized waiting is monotone in length, so the second distinct hop count yields the second distinct arrival time.
editorial: Two-distance BFS enumerates walk lengths in order; deterministic synchronized waiting is monotone in length, so the second distinct hop count yields the second distinct arrival time.

tests.explanation: The second distinct arrival reaches vertex five at time thirteen.
The second route revisits the first vertex and reaches the destination at time eleven.
